stem.text: Find the value of \( \lim_{x \to 1} \frac{x \ln x - x + 1}{x^{3} - 2x^{2} + x} \).

worked_solution.text: As \( x \to 1 \), the numerator \( x \ln x - x + 1 \) tends to \( 0 \).
As \( x \to 1 \), the denominator \( x^{3} - 2x^{2} + x \) tends to \( 0 \).

The numerator and the denominator both tend to 0, so the form is \( \frac{0}{0} \) and L'Hospital's rule applies. Differentiate the numerator and the denominator separately: the limit equals \( \lim_{x \to 1} \frac{\ln x}{3x^{2} - 4x + 1} \).

The new numerator and denominator both tend to 0 again, so the form is still \( \frac{0}{0} \) and the rule applies once more. Differentiate each separately again: the limit equals \( \lim_{x \to 1} \frac{\frac{1}{x}}{6x - 4} \).
At \( x = 1 \) this numerator is \( 1 \) and this denominator is \( 2 \), which is not 0, so the limit is \( \frac{1}{2} \).
